reason: Both wrongly started with the belt and both over-applied a stop-use banner to a faint smell weeks ago, but Conversation 1 reached the correct, honest outcome: worn/charred brushes, replace as a pair, DIY-appropriate with a matching kit, engineer as an option — matching the expected direction. Conversation 2 identified the same cause yet then insisted the machine 'must not be used until checked by a qualified engineer', denying the homeowner a reasonable £10-£20 DIY fix, giving no part advice, and nudging toward replacement; it was also self-contradictory by having the owner strip the motor while declaring it engineer-only. Conversation 2 did better on process (unplug, pull out, get the full model number) and 1 was slightly overconfident ('that confirms it') and omitted the 'if new brushes don't fix it, call an engineer' fallback, so the margin is only slight.
